destino.area: Kaa-Iya del Gran Chaco National Park and Integrated Management Natural Area

modalidad: Niche ecotourism, active conservation and ethical wildlife tracking

hero.bajada: Join an exclusive expedition to spot the last population of Chaco guanacos in the largest tropical dry forest on Earth.
hero.alt: Chaco guanaco among the dry scrubland of the Gran Chaco

experiencia.titulo: An expedition to see the guanaco without disturbing it
experiencia.introduccion: We search for the Chaco guanaco in the open scrublands of Kaa-Iya, reading tracks and signs, and watch it from a distance with long-range optics.

destacado.texto: Chaco guanacos survive in Bolivia. They are the country’s last lowland population, and they are critically endangered.

puntos.descripcion: We read fresh tracks and signs of movement, then observe through high-definition binoculars and 20–60x spotting scopes, always from a safe distance.

puntos.titulo: The only trip built around the guanaco
puntos.descripcion: Other Kaa-Iya expeditions chase the jaguar. This is the only one in Bolivia dedicated to the lowland guanaco.
You log your sightings and geotagged photos on iNaturalist and eBird, adding data that supports monitoring of the species.

guanaco.titulo: Seen through a scope, never up close
guanaco.texto: Chaco guanacos are wary, and the population is tiny. We track them by their prints and watch from a safe distance through 20–60x spotting scopes, so they keep grazing as if we weren’t there.
guanaco.alt: Small group of Chaco guanacos grazing in open scrubland

actividades.descripcion: We cross the Gran Chaco in vehicles equipped for wildlife viewing: guanacos, tapirs, Chacoan peccaries, capuchin monkeys and armadillos. After dark, we look for signs of jaguar and puma.
actividades.alt: 4x4 vehicle on a dirt track in the Gran Chaco

actividades.descripcion: We camp under some of the darkest skies in the Southern Hemisphere, perfect for photographing constellations and the Milky Way.
actividades.alt: Starry sky over the camp in the dry forest

actividades.descripcion: We settle quietly near natural waterholes, where wildlife comes to drink in the first hours of the morning.
actividades.alt: Waterhole at sunrise surrounded by Chaco vegetation

actividades.descripcion: A guided walk through dry-forest flora: white quebracho, cuchi, toborochi (silk floss tree), palo santo and giant cacti.
actividades.alt: Toborochi tree and cacti in the Chaco dry forest

galeria.intro: The guanaco is why we go, but along the way you may also spot these.

imagenes.alt: Lowland tapir walking through dry forest
Capuchin monkey on a tree branch
Jaguar paw print in the sand
Palm groves silhouetted at sunset in the Chaco

itinerario.introduccion: Two days timed to the hours when wildlife is most active: afternoon and night safaris, and sunrise at the waterholes.

dias.titulo: Into the Gran Chaco: 4x4 safari and astrophotography

bloques.titulo: Departure from Santa Cruz and drive to the Chaco region
bloques.descripcion: Private transfer in 4x4 vehicles, with an introductory briefing on Leave No Trace principles.
Park entry paperwork and a ceremony of respect for the Kaa-Iya, the “Lord of the Forest,” with the park rangers.
Lunch at Tucavaca Camp and dust-proofing cameras and optics.

bloques.titulo: 4x4 photo safari and search for the Chaco guanaco
bloques.descripcion: An intensive drive along the right-of-way searching for guanaco herds and other iconic mammals.
We pitch the tents and shoot the golden hour over the palm groves.

bloques.titulo: Night safari for big cats and astrophotography
bloques.descripcion: A night drive looking for signs of jaguar and puma, plus stargazing. Overnight in tents.

dias.titulo: Waterhole watch and native plant tracking

bloques.titulo: Morning watch at the waterholes and wildlife monitoring
bloques.descripcion: We position ourselves at natural waterholes to observe wildlife coming to drink.
A second search for guanacos and a guided walk through endemic plants such as palo santo (Bulnesia sarmientoi) and giant cacti. Then we break camp.

ruta.alt: Illustrated route map from Santa Cruz de la Sierra through San José de Chiquitos, Taperas and Roboré to the base camp and the high guanaco activity zone
ruta.leyenda: Route from Santa Cruz de la Sierra to the high guanaco activity zone.

paradas.detalle: End of pavement, start of the 4x4 trail
Walking routes, guanaco tracks, wildlife and plants

alojamiento.titulo: No hotel rooms here: we sleep under the stars
alojamiento.descripcion: You’ll spend the night in tents at a camp inside the protected area. We bring all the expedition gear, so you only need your clothes and a warm layer.
puntos: Tents and expedition camping gear included
Full meals prepared by cooks from San José de Chiquitos
Days can top 104 °F (40 °C) and nights get cool: bring a warm layer

sostenibilidad.introduccion: The expedition is designed so Kaa-Iya stays as we found it, and so conservation benefits the people who live in the Chaco.

compromisos.descripcion: We only use routes authorized by SERNAP, Bolivia’s protected areas service, to prevent erosion and disturbance. All waste leaves the park with us.

We work with rangers from the Charagua Iyambae Indigenous Autonomy and with guides, drivers and cooks from San José de Chiquitos. Local jobs give communities a reason to protect the guanaco instead of hunting it.

items: Bilingual naturalist guide and local guide
All field meals and drinking water
Use of binoculars and spotting scopes
A warm layer for the night
Certified drivers and vehicles with preventive maintenance
Guides with WFR certification and a first-aid kit
Daily weather and wildfire monitoring, with rescheduling if access closes
